Definition: of Hebrew origin (H4442); Melchisedek (i.e. Malkitsedek), a patriarch:--Melchisedec.
BiblicalUsage: Melchisedek is the king of Salem and priest of the most high God, and Hebrews holds him up as the pattern of Christ's priesthood. Hebrews 7:1 tells how he met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him, and Hebrews 5:6 and Hebrews 7:17 both quote the promise, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Melchizedek matters because he shows a priesthood older than Aaron and higher than Levi: a king who is also priest, with no beginning of days in the record, pointing straight to Christ. My position is that Hebrews is right to rest everything on him, because a priest who lives for ever is the only priest we need.
